reasoning_traces.think:
The core operation of 3DPCNet is a canonical transformation defined by \(\hat{X}_c = \hat{R}^\top X + \Delta\), where \(\hat{R}\) is a predicted global rotation matrix and \(\Delta\) is a per-joint residual. The rotation is computed from a 6D vector using Gram–Schmidt orthogonalization to ensure SO(3) membership. This mapping is invariant to viewpoint because it aligns all poses to a fixed canonical reference frame. The module assumes that viewpoint variation is primarily rigid and that ground-truth canonical frames are available during training through synthetic rotations. Failure occurs when input poses are inaccurate or when \(\Delta\) introduces distortions that compromise biomechanical fidelity. Temporal consistency is absent in the base model, leading to jittery rotations. The model is estimator-agnostic, meaning it can process outputs from any 3D pose estimator without retraining. However, this also implies that errors in the upstream estimator propagate into canonical space unless corrected. In GSI, this framework supports robust uncertainty quantification in biomechanical metrics. In GSE, it provides a preprocessing layer to stabilize pose tracking across multi-camera NFL footage.
